Dear list,

I have two dataframes: trans and peakdata.

 > dput (trans)
structure(list(loc = c(1, 3, 18, 15, 22, 34, 50, 43, 90), fc = c(3.2,
4.5, 1.4, 1.1, 4.7, 5.1, 2, 5.2, 3.5)), .Names = c("loc", "fc"
), row.names = c(NA, -9L), class = "data.frame")
> dput (peakdata)
structure(list(start = c(2, 10, 20, 45), end = c(4, 15, 21, 60
), testpeak = c(2, 5, 2, 7)), .Names = c("start", "end", "testpeak"
), row.names = c(NA, -4L), class = "data.frame")


I would like to plot them, principally this way:

> qm <- ggplot (trans, aes(x=loc, y=fc))+ geom_point ()+geom_segment (data=peakdata, aes(x=start, xend=end, yend=0, y=testpeak), color="red")

Of course it would be much better to do it via faceting but I did not find a proper example for this using different dataframes. Could you please give me some instructions?
Thanks
Hermann

messages.subject: Re: faceting with different data frames
parts:
When faceting the facets generally have to have the same x and y axis. If one of your axes is a factor you can have it leave out unused levels per facet or adjust to fit the space if your values per facet are numerically very different, but if you want to facet something that shares an x, but not a y... I'm not sure. 

That's probably better done using grid/gridExtra to layout the two plots on top of each other. You could cheat if both Y's are numerical, but then you'd run into issues labeling your y-axis, what units go with which facet? 

Perhaps others have better ideas? 

B

On Fri, Oct 5, 2012 at 11:27 AM, Hermann Norpois <hnor...@googlemail.com> wrote:
Sorry for being vague.

The point is that both data sets share the same x axes but have different y axes. So I wish to have two different coordinate systems (one above the other). So far I was not able to do so. In my example both data sets are plotted in one coordinate system.

Thanks.
